title: QBR KPI heuristics and templates - labbook
summary: Working labbook for defining QBR-level KPI definitions and templated tables that we can drop into account review decks. Focus: practical measurement (how we compute each metric), heuristics for setting targets, and a renewal scoring mapping that mixes latency, uptime, cost/token and cache behavior.
body:
Purpose and audience:
- Audience: CSMs preparing QBR decks, Solutions Engs preparing renewal recommendations, and Product Ops who maintain metric queries.
- Purpose: give reproducible definitions (numerator/denominator), query hints, and a standard KPI table + notes so each account review is consistent and defensible.

Tone: labbook/draft. Include example queries and open items for SRE/observability.

High-level principle:
- Keep definitions implementable by a single metric query. If approximations are used (e.g., synthetic vs production traffic), annotate.
- Prefer percentiles for latency (p50/p95/p99) and absolute SLO for uptime.
- Cost metrics must include clear tokenization and billing assumptions (encoder vs decoder tokens).

Metric definitions (implementation-minded):
1) Request latency (per-request tokenization-aware)
- Definition: latency = time between request received by inference gateway and final token emitted OR final response completed (use whichever is used in product path).
- Primary views: p50, p95, p99 for end-to-end latency; mean for long-running batch jobs.
- Example metric names to query: redwood.inference.request_latency_ms (tags: model, route, customer_id, success).
- Example query (pseudo-SQL / metric DSL):
  SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 50) as p50, percentile(latency_ms, 95) as p95, percentile(latency_ms, 99) as p99
  FROM requests
  WHERE customer_id = '<account>' AND timeframe = 'last_30d' AND success = true
- Heuristics: use rolling 30d for QBR summary; show last-week trend for anomalies. For chat/streaming flows also show median time-to-first-byte.

2) Uptime (service + model variant)
- Definition: uptime = 1 - (total_error_seconds / total_observation_seconds) over reporting window. Distinguish platform availability (gateway + control plane) vs model-serving availability (model process crashes, OOMs, eviction).
- Important labels: route, region, model_variant, deployment_tier (hosted/dedicated/private).
- SLO framing: platform-level target (e.g., 99.9% monthly), model-variant-level softer target (e.g., 99.5% monthly) depending on SLAs.
- Example metric: redwood.inference.error_seconds and redwood.inference.observation_seconds or synthetics: redwood.synthetic.ping_failed.

3) Cost per token (normalized)
- Definition: cost/token = total_inference_cost_in_usd / total_billed_tokens. Must state tokenization: use BPE counts from tokenizer vX (link tokenizer reference). Separate encoder vs decoder tokens if model charges differ.
- Implementation detail: prefer cost models aggregated from chargeback pipeline (billing exports) over raw infra cost unless billing export not available. Document assumptions if using infra estimate (GPU-hours * instance_price / tokens_generated).
- Example: Cost assumptions used for this QBR: tokenizer=v0.2, bill_tokens = encoder_tokens + decoder_tokens, platform_charge = usage_report.

4) Cache hit rate (prefix/KV cache)
- Definition: cache_hit_rate = cached_responses_served / total_requests_eligible_for_cache. Must define "eligible": requests where cache_key was present (e.g., same prompt fingerprint or same prompt+context hash) and response could be reused.
- Important to include TTL behavior, partial-hit semantics (e.g., prefix-kv partial reuse).
- Example metrics: redwood.cache.request_eligible_total, redwood.cache.hits.
- Caveat: high cache hit rate generally reduces cost and p50 latency, but can mask quality regressions if cached responses are stale post-rollout. Recommend showing percent of hits from cached canonical outputs vs from fallback model variants.

KPI presentation template (single table for QBR deck) - canonical columns and explanation (this is the templated copy you can paste):
KPI | Numerator | Denominator | Window | Owner | QBR target | Alert threshold | Notes
- Request latency (p95 ms) | p95 latency_ms | all successful requests | 30d | eng-sre/customer-success | <= 350 ms | > 600 ms | show trend sparkline + last-week delta
- Uptime (platform %) | observation_seconds - error_seconds | observation_seconds | 90d | eng-sre | >= 99.9% | < 99.5% | split by region; call out private deployments separately
- Cost per 1k tokens (USD) | sum(inference_cost_usd) * 1000 | sum(billed_tokens) | 30d | finance + product | account-specific goal | 25% above baseline | include tokenization note
- Cache hit rate (%) | cache_hits | cache_eligible_requests | 30d | product/solutions | >= 40% (if cacheable workload) | < 20% | indicate cache TTL and eviction reasons

Sample KPI table (text version you can paste into slides):
- Request latency (p95 ms): 420 ms (30d avg), +12% vs prior 30d, alert=600ms
- Uptime (platform 90d): 99.92%, incidents: 2 (one model eviction), action: increase reserved capacity for region
- Cost/1k tokens: $1.76 (billing export), tokenizer=v0.2 accounted; note heavy decoder usage drives up cost
- Cache hit rate: 33%, TTL average 6h, partial hits account for 8% of hits

Renewal scoring heuristic (example weight-based mapping to be adapted per account):
- Overall renewal_score (0-100) = 0.4 * latency_score + 0.3 * uptime_score + 0.2 * cost_score + 0.1 * cache_score
- Score buckets (per metric):
  latency_score = 100 if p95 <= target, 50 if p95 between target and 2x target, 0 if > 2x target
  uptime_score = 100 if uptime >= target, 60 if within 0.2% below target, 0 if >1% below target
  cost_score = 100 if cost <= committed baseline, 50 if within 25% above baseline, 0 if >50% above baseline
  cache_score = linear 0-100 where >= target yields 100, 0 at 0% hits
- Example: Account A with p95=420ms (target 350) -> latency_score 50; uptime 99.92 (target 99.9) -> uptime_score 100; cost 1.76 vs baseline 1.40 -> cost_score 50; cache 33 vs target 40 -> cache_score 82 -> overall ~0.4*50+0.3*100+0.2*50+0.1*82 = 63.2 -> classify: at-risk but engage/solutions-engine for cost optimization and latency tuning.

Operational notes and query hints (for Product Ops / SRE):
- When building queries, join billing export by invoice_run_id for stable cost windows; avoid mixing calendar and billing windows without annotation.
- For latency percentiles, prefer histogram-based metrics with reservoir sampling, avoid computing percentiles client-side on raw events which can be heavy.
- Annotate rollouts: any model rollout during the window should be a callout row in the QBR; include release tag and time. Cached responses created before a rollout should be excluded from post-rollout quality analyses.

Template snippets (copyable) - Prometheus/metric-dsl pseudocode:
- p95 latency last 30d: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_latency_bucket[30d])) by (le, customer_id))
- cache hit rate: sum(redwood_cache_hits{customer_id="<id>"}) / sum(redwood_cache_eligible{customer_id="<id>"})
- cost per token (billing export): sum(billing.charge_usd{customer_id="<id>"}) / sum(billing.tokens{customer_id="<id>"})

Labbook notes / open items (actionable):
- We need SRE to validate observation_seconds metric for private deployments (owner: Samir Khan).
- Confirm tokenizer v0.2 mapping to billed tokens in billing export (owner: Evan Morales).
- Add synthetic-first-byte metric for streaming routes to highlight slow start vs slow tail (suggested instrumentation: redwood.inference.time_to_first_byte_ms).
- Decide on consistent QBR windows (30d vs 90d) per KPI; proposal: latency and cost = 30d, uptime = 90d, cache = 30d.

Notes to self (Aisha):
- For next iteration, build a small exporter that emits computed KPI rows per account to a single dataset so CSMs can fetch a canonical row for their deck.
- Try to capture partial-cache semantics (how often cache reduces token generation vs returns entire cached payload).

Appendix: short glossary
- Billed tokens: tokens counted by billing export (may differ from tokenizer tool output).
- Eligible-for-cache: request fingerprint matched preconditions for cache reuse.
- Model variant: a specific model + quantization combo used in serving.

End of labbook.

renewal_scoring: Renewal score formula: 0.4*latency + 0.3*uptime + 0.2*cost + 0.1*cache. Provide numeric example for Account A and mapping to bucket (engage, monitor, at-risk). Include call to action recommendations per bucket.
open_questions:
- Who owns the canonical tokenizer mapping used by billing export? (owner: Evan)
- Should we automatically exclude cached responses from quality evals after rollouts?
- Agree on QBR windows (30d vs 90d) in policy doc?
- How to present partial-cache benefit in a succinct chart (tokens saved vs requests)?
